#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify the frozen export and source repository against the pinned identity.

Usage: verify_identity.py IDENTITY_JSON EXPORT_DIR SOURCE_REPO
Checks:
  1. export path set == manifest paths + {north-star.json} (+ review-evidence/ ignored)
  2. every export file SHA256 == manifest
  3. every export file git-blob hash (sha1 "blob N\\0") == pinned git_blobs
  4. source repo `git ls-tree -r <commit>` path->blob == pinned git_blobs
  5. source repo HEAD == commit and `git status --porcelain` output (reported)
"""
import hashlib, json, os, subprocess, sys

ident_path, export, repo = sys.argv[1:4]
ident = json.load(open(ident_path))
files, blobs, commit = ident["files"], ident["git_blobs"], ident["commit"]
ok = True

def fail(msg):
    global ok
    ok = False
    print("FAIL", msg)

if set(files) != set(blobs):
    fail("manifest files/git_blobs key sets differ")

seen = set()
for root, dirs, names in os.walk(export):
    rel_root = os.path.relpath(root, export)
    if rel_root == "review-evidence" or rel_root.startswith("review-evidence" + os.sep):
        dirs[:] = []
        continue
    for n in names:
        p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(rel_root, n))
        seen.add(p)
extra = sorted(seen - set(files))
missing = sorted(set(files) - seen)
print("export_files", len(seen), "manifest_files", len(files))
print("extra", extra)
print("missing", missing)
if extra != ["north-star.json"]:
    fail("unexpected extra set %r" % extra)
if missing:
    fail("missing files")

sha_bad = blob_bad = 0
for p in sorted(set(files) & seen):
    full = os.path.join(export, p)
    if os.path.islink(full):
        data = os.readlink(full).encode()
    else:
        data = open(full, "rb").read()
    if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != files[p]:
        sha_bad += 1
        fail("sha256 mismatch " + p)
    gb = hashlib.sha1(b"blob %d\0" % len(data) + data).hexdigest()
    if gb != blobs[p]:
        blob_bad += 1
        fail("git blob mismatch " + p)
print("sha256_mismatches", sha_bad, "blob_mismatches", blob_bad)

out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", commit],
                     capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
tree = {}
for ent in out.split(b"\0"):
    if not ent:
        continue
    meta, path = ent.split(b"\t", 1)
    mode, typ, obj = meta.split()
    tree[path.decode()] = obj.decode()
if tree != blobs:
    d1 = set(tree) ^ set(blobs)
    d2 = [p for p in set(tree) & set(blobs) if tree[p] != blobs[p]]
    fail("commit tree != pinned blobs: pathdiff=%r blobdiff=%r" % (sorted(d1)[:20], d2[:20]))
print("commit_tree_entries", len(tree), "matches_pinned", tree == blobs)
head = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
print("source_HEAD", head, "pinned", commit, "equal", head == commit)
if head != commit:
    fail("HEAD differs")
st = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=no"],
                    capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
print("source_tracked_status_porcelain", repr(st))
if st:
    fail("source tracked tree dirty")
print("RESULT", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

The fold reads morphisms; it never mutates objects. **No operation destroys a

If a change would let one actor's write mutate or destroy another's data, it's wrong.

Local-only, one human, one-or-more local agents, one repo, no sync:
Claim + DAG-CBOR CID + signing → local append-only log (source of truth) →
disposable SQLite index → the fold (identity-before-state, same enrichment,
decategorify only at render) → git anchors + computable relation providers →
CLI + MCP server with budgeted context assembly.

Explicitly OUT for the local spine: sync/atproto/lexicons, TUI, web dashboard,
editor extensions, >2 trust enrichments, enforcement hooks, incremental fold.
The local-only spine shipped through v0.3.0-beta.1. Do not treat that historical

current plan. Read `docs/ROADMAP.md` first for sync-adjacent work; public

---
name: adversarial-review
allowed-tools: Bash(kan *), Bash(day *), Bash(git *), Bash(gh *), Bash(cargo *), Bash(npm *), Bash(make *), Bash(ls *), Bash(rg *), Read, Grep, Glob
description: Hostile-by-default post-implementation audit against a named north star, ending in a hard verdict
---

> **day's "adversarial review" atom** (`docs/TELOS.md`). Its interface: it
> consumes an implementation plus the design document that intended it, and
> produces a verdict claim recorded in kan.
>
> ```day-atom
> {"_version": 2, "in": ["code-change", "design-doc"], "out": ["verdict"],
>  "next": ["pull-request"], "revisits": ["generative-build"]}
> ```
>
> Adapted from `forecast-bio/crosslink`'s `architect` skill (its
> "Checkpoint 2 — post-implementation audit"), redesigned around kan's
> actual model: this reviews **what is already on disk or merged**, not a
> pending subagent dispatch.

## Context — gather this yourself, and report what fails

Run these before Step 0. **A read that fails is a finding, not an empty
result**, and this section is instructions rather than pre-expanded output
because of what happened here specifically. day#100: the telos line grepped a
shape `kan status` no longer emits, matched nothing, its fallback printed
`none`, and **every adversarial review in this repo silently measured against
`CLAUDE.md` instead of nine live teloi**, exit zero throughout. A review whose
north star is wrong is worse than no review, and nothing about that failure was
visible from inside it.

- **Repo root** — `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
  **If this read fails:** you are not in a git repo, so there is no diff to
  review. Say so and ask what to audit rather than reviewing the working
  directory.
- **Branch** — `git branch --show-current`.
  **If this read fails:** or prints nothing, you are on a detached HEAD. Name
  the commit range explicitly instead of assuming one.
- **Diff under review** — `git diff --stat main...HEAD`.
  **If this read fails:** there is no `main` to compare against. Say which range
  you used instead and why; a review of the wrong range is worse than no review,
  and this is the sentence that stops that being silent.
- **Design docs** — `ls .design/*.md`.
  **If this read fails:** there are no design docs, so Step 2's REQ/AC table has
  nothing to audit against. Report that as the finding — unstated intent is
  where drift enters — rather than inventing requirements.
- **Teloi in play** — `kan show --all --json`, filtered to subjects beginning
  `telos/`. Use the bulk verb: `kan show <subject>` is O(n²) in commit-anchored
  claims and was measured at 141 s where `--all --json` takes 72 ms (kan#181).
  **If this read fails:** kan is not on PATH or the log is unreadable. **Say
  that, and do not fall through to the orientation-file branch in Step 1** — a
  failed read and a project with no teloi are different states, and treating the
  first as the second is day#100 exactly. An *empty* result is also not "no
  teloi" until you have confirmed the log is readable and simply has none.
- **Orientation files** — `ls *.md docs/*.md`.
  **If this read fails:** say so; Step 1's fallback then has no source either,
  and a review with no north star at all should stop and ask for one.

The telos list you assemble is **subjects on record, not teloi in play** — it
does not filter retracted ones, and day's own reader does
(`src/hooks.rs:render_teloi`). Step 1 says how to narrow it.

## Your task

You are an **independent, hostile-by-default reviewer**. You did not write this
code and you have no stake in it having gone well. Your default posture is that
the implementation drifted from its intent in ways its author cannot see, because
that is the common case, not the exceptional one.

You are not here to be encouraging. You are here to find the gap between what was
meant and what exists, and to say so plainly.

### Step 0 — Establish that you are that reviewer

Read this before Step 1. If you wrote any of the code under review, **every
clause of the paragraph above is false about you**: you did write it, you have
just reported it complete, and you carry the reasoning this review exists to
audit from the outside.

That is the default case when this command is invoked as a slash command in the
session that produced the work, so treat it as the expected situation, not an
edge case.

1. **Where the harness can dispatch a fresh agent, offer to.** Hand it the design
   doc, the kan subject, and the diff range, and let it report back. In Claude
   Code that is the Agent tool with a **general-purpose** agent.
2. **It must be cold, not a fork.** `subagent_type: "fork"` inherits the parent's
   full conversation, so it arrives already holding the rationalisations this
   step exists to strip. It would reproduce the problem while appearing to solve
   it. A context-inheriting reviewer is not an independent one.
3. **Offer, do not force.** An in-context pass is fast and catches the obvious,
   and the operator may legitimately want one. Ask; abide by the answer.
4. **If you proceed in-context — because the operator declined, or because no
   such capability exists — say so in your output, in the verdict itself**, in
   roughly this form:

   > **Declared conflict of interest.** The premise of this review is a reviewer
   > with no stake. I wrote this code. I have compensated by reproducing every
   > claim against the running binary rather than by reading my own tests, but an
   > independent reviewer would still be better placed to find what follows.

   A review that is not independent and does not say so is worse than an openly
   self-audited one, because the verdict reads identically either way.

This is not ceremony. Two of the three defects behind day#101 were found by a
review of code the same session had written, and both were found by *executing*
it against hostile input rather than by re-reading it — which is the step an
author is least likely to take, because they already believe they know what it
does. When you cannot get independence, buy back what it was protecting: run the
thing, do not re-read your own summary of it.

### Arguments

- `--design <slug>`: the design doc to audit against (`.design/<slug>.md`)
- `--subject <subject>`: the kan subject carrying this work's claims
- `--pr <number>`: audit a GitHub PR's diff instead of the working branch

If none are given, infer the target from the branch and the most recently modified
design doc, and **state the inference explicitly** before proceeding — a review of
the wrong thing is worse than no review.

### Step 1 — Recite the north star, from the record

Do not paraphrase from memory and do not invent a north star.

1. If any `telos/*` subjects exist in kan, read them (`kan show telos/<slug>`).
   Those are the north star. Quote them.

   **What you gathered is subjects on record, not teloi in play.** It does not
   filter retracted ones; day's own reader does
   (`src/hooks.rs:render_teloi`), and the two lists differ in this repo
   today. A retracted telos quoted as the north star is a review measuring
   against a target the project abandoned — so confirm each one is live, and
   treat the list as a starting set, not an answer.
2. If none exist, fall back to this repo's orientation docs (`CLAUDE.md`, an
   authoritative spec, the design doc's own Summary). Quote the specific lines.

   Before you take that branch: **"none" here has three causes** — a project with
   no teloi, a log you could not read, and a filter that no longer matches what
   kan emits. Only the first licenses the fallback. The third is what happened
   here once already, and it reported `none` in a repo with nine live teloi,
   silently, for as long as nobody checked; the second is the reason the Context
   section tells you to report a failed kan read rather than continue past it.
   Confirm the log is readable and genuinely empty of `telos/` subjects before
   concluding there is no north star.
3. State which telos or stated purpose **this particular work** was meant to
   serve. If you cannot find one, that is itself a finding: record it and say
   so — unstated purpose is where drift enters.

Where several teloi are in play, name the tension between them. Work that
silently optimizes one at another's expense is the single most common real
finding this review produces.

### Step 2 — REQ/AC coverage table

For each REQ and AC in the design doc, produce a row: the requirement, the
verdict (`met` / `partial` / `unmet` / `unverifiable`), and **the evidence**.

Evidence means a file path and line range you actually read, or command output
you actually ran. It does not mean:

- the design doc asserting its own requirement is satisfied,
- a commit message, changelog entry, or ADR saying the work was done,
- an agent's summary of what it did.

Quote the code. If a requirement's satisfaction cannot be established from the
artifacts, mark it `unverifiable` and say what would be needed — never round it
up to `met`.

### Step 3 — Verify the evidence yourself

Run the project's own verification, in this order, and report raw results:

1. Build (`cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, `npm run build`, `make`, …)
2. Tests (`cargo test --workspace`, `npm test`, …)
3. Lint (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, …)
4. Format (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, …)

If a claimed test exists, **run that specific test and confirm it fails when the
behavior is broken** where you can do so cheaply. A test that passes
unconditionally is not coverage. If you cannot run something, say so — do not
report unrun commands as passing.

### Step 4 — Scope-narrowing check

Grep the diff, the design doc, and any new decision records for scope-narrowing
language: `out of scope`, `deferred`, `follow-up`, `future work`, `for now`,
`TODO`, `later`, `v2`.

Judge each instance independently:

- **Legitimate**: named before implementation, recorded, and genuinely separable.
- **Suspicious**: narrowed *during* implementation, or narrowing exactly the part
  that was hard, or deferring the requirement that made the feature worth doing.

Quote each instance and give a verdict per instance. A design that ended up
smaller than it started is not automatically wrong, but it needs to have been
decided, not drifted into.

### Step 5 — Forbidden-pattern re-introduction

Check the diff against this repo's own stated house rules — the ones in its
`CLAUDE.md` and its decision records, not generic best practice. For kan and day
specifically, that includes:

- The fold reads; it never mutates. No operation destroys a subject.
- Affordance, not enforcement — no blocking hooks, no gates on agent action.
- One surface (CLI + MCP); no second UI sneaking in.
- Provenance is sacred: `cites` edges are never fabricated or dropped.
- day stores nothing of its own; durable state is kan claims.

For any other repo, derive the equivalent list from its own docs and say which
rules you derived and from where.

### Step 6 — Verdict

End with **exactly one** of these four, in bold, with a one-paragraph rationale:

- **APPROVE** — requirements met, evidence verified independently, no drift.
- **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS** — sound and shippable; specific, named gaps that
  do not undermine the north star. List them as concrete follow-ups.
- **REDIRECT** — the work is competent but pointed somewhere other than the
  stated telos. Say precisely where it diverged and what it should serve instead.
- **BLOCK** — a correctness, safety, or invariant violation. Name the invariant
  and the exact code that violates it.

Do not soften the verdict to be agreeable. Do not inflate it to seem rigorous.
"APPROVE" on genuinely good work is a useful signal that only stays useful if
you are willing to say it.

### Step 7 — Record it

```bash
day review record <subject> \
  --verdict APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOW-UPS \
  --rationale "<one line>" \
  --cites <cid of the design/plan claim being audited>
```

The verdict must be one of the four values above and must cite the claim it
audits; `day` rejects anything else rather than recording a verdict nobody can
trace back to what it judged.

Record each material finding as its own claim citing that verdict, so a later
session can find the finding without re-reading this whole review:

```bash
kan observe "<finding>" --subject <subject> --cites "$VERDICT"
```

If the verdict is BLOCK or REDIRECT, also mark the subject:

```bash
kan mark <subject> --value Blocked   # check `kan mark --help` for valid values
```

### Step 8 — What comes next

```bash
day next adversarial-review
```

Report what the graph says rather than naming a step from memory. A project
that loops review back into design has declared that; another may terminate
here.

**A round of fixes to a BLOCK gets its own review** — kan's ADR-52, stated here
rather than left as something a person has to remember. It has now been
validated **eight times** in this repo, and three times consecutively in one
milestone, where each round found defects the previous round's author could not
see. The severity moved as it went: round 1 found code defects, round 2 found a
bug the round-1 fix introduced, and round 3 found that *"the code changes in this
round are correct… what is wrong is the evidence."*

So when this review returns BLOCK, the fixes are a new implementation, not an
addendum to the reviewed one, and they are reviewed as such. The author of a fix
round is the least able person to see what it missed, which is the same argument
that makes this atom cold in the first place (Step 0).

If the fix round closes a finding, its commit carries a `Demonstrated-by:`
trailer from `scripts/revert-demo.py` — revert the fix, watch the named test
fail, restore, watch it pass. A round that says "fixed and the suite is green"
has asserted the weaker of the two things, and day#116's first instance is a fix
whose entire reversion left 337/337 tests passing.

## Rules

- **Probes leave traces.** Verifying a defect by running the real command
  against the real log appends real claims — that is how a junk
  `telos/review-probe` subject ended up in day's own record and then in its
  session-start context. Probe in a scratch repo, or retract in the same
  breath. An assessment that pollutes the record it assesses is measuring its
  own footprint.
- **Check the other side of every interface.** The most serious finding this
  review has produced was a hook wired to an event whose stdout never reaches
  the model — invisible to every test, because the tests asserted what the
  tool printed rather than whether anything read it. Read the docs for the
  thing being integrated with; do not infer its behavior from your own side.
- Do NOT modify code. This atom reads and judges; fixing is a separate atom.
- Do NOT trust the design doc, the ADRs, or the commit messages about whether
  the work was done. They are claims about the work, not the work.
- Do NOT report a command as run if you did not run it.
- Every finding cites a file path and line, or command output.
- If the design doc itself is wrong or incoherent, say that — auditing against a
  bad specification faithfully is still a failed review.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+
+def generate():
+    cases=[]
+    for name,original,restore in [
+        ('E1-empty-original-initial-loss',b'',False),

+        if restore:history.restore(cid,b'correct')
+        encoded=history.encoded()
+        packed=rv.members.pack(name,member,observer,complete=rv.complete(member))
+        rv.replay(history,encoded)
+        cases.append({'name':name,'member':packed,'candidates':[[cid,b.hex()] for cid,b in history.candidates],
+            'observations':[b.hex() for b in encoded],'checkpoint':history.checkpoint,
+            'designExpect':'accept','pythonOracle':'accept'})
+    for restore in [False,True]:
+        name='E5-partial-profile3-empty-original-restored' if restore else 'E4-partial-profile3-empty-original-initial-loss'
+        member,observer=rv.members.build(3,3);member['records']=member['records'][:1]
+        cid,correct=member['objects'][0];member['objects'][0]=[cid,b'']
+        history=rv.History(member,observer);history.initial()

+        encoded=history.encoded();rv.replay(history,encoded)
+        packed=rv.members.pack(name,member,observer,complete=False)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reproduce three independent review probes and add partial-profile-3 coverage.
+
+The raw reviewer generator is retained separately. This promoted generator uses
+its same signed history construction and compares the exact fixture bytes.
+Physical files are produced by recovery_bundle_files.py; no Rust or live data.
+"""
+import argparse,json
+from pathlib import Path
+import recovery_replay_vectors as rv
+ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+TARGET=ROOT/'.design/fixtures/recovery-bundle-review-v1.json'
+
+def generate():
+    cases=[]
+    for name,original,restore in [
+        ('E1-empty-original-initial-loss',b'',False),
+        ('E2-empty-original-restored',b'',True),
+        ('E3-nonempty-corrupt-original-restored-control',b'x',True),
+    ]:
+        member,observer=rv.members.build(2,0)
+        cid=rv.frame.raw_cid(b'correct');member['objects']=[[cid,original]]
+        history=rv.History(member,observer);history.initial()
+        if restore:history.restore(cid,b'correct')
+        encoded=history.encoded()
+        packed=rv.members.pack(name,member,observer,complete=rv.complete(member))
+        rv.replay(history,encoded)
+        cases.append({'name':name,'member':packed,'candidates':[[cid,b.hex()] for cid,b in history.candidates],
+            'observations':[b.hex() for b in encoded],'checkpoint':history.checkpoint,
+            'designExpect':'accept','pythonOracle':'accept'})
+    for restore in [False,True]:
+        name='E5-partial-profile3-empty-original-restored' if restore else 'E4-partial-profile3-empty-original-initial-loss'
+        member,observer=rv.members.build(3,3);member['records']=member['records'][:1]
+        cid,correct=member['objects'][0];member['objects'][0]=[cid,b'']
+        history=rv.History(member,observer);history.initial()
+        if restore:history.restore(cid,correct)
+        encoded=history.encoded();rv.replay(history,encoded)
+        packed=rv.members.pack(name,member,observer,complete=False)
+        cases.append({'name':name,'member':packed,'candidates':[[cid,b.hex()] for cid,b in history.candidates],
+            'observations':[b.hex() for b in encoded],'checkpoint':history.checkpoint,
+            'designExpect':'accept','pythonOracle':'accept'})
+    return json.dumps({'cases':cases},indent=1)
+
+def main():
+    p=argparse.ArgumentParser();p.add_argument('--check',action='store_true');a=p.parse_args();text=generate()
+    if a.check:
+        if TARGET.read_text()!=text:raise SystemExit('promoted recovery-bundle vectors differ')
+        print('Five empty/corrupt-original vectors reproduce; original three reviewer cases retained unchanged')
+    else:TARGET.write_text(text)
+if __name__=='__main__':main()

import json

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reviewer probe generator (independent of the author's corpus selection).
Builds signed histories with the repo's public test-key primitives and writes
physical KNB1 files with the author's fixture constructor. Expectations come
from the design text, not Rust. Usage: gen_physical_probes.py OUT_DIR
"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, sqlite3, shutil
from pathlib import Path
EXPORT = Path(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else Path.cwd()
TOOLS = EXPORT / '.design/tools'
sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))
import recovery_replay_vectors as rv
import recovery_bundle_files as rbf
members, frame, codec = rv.members, rv.frame, rv.codec
out = Path(sys.argv[1]); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
cases = []
def add(name, h, design_expect):
    env = h.encoded()
    c = {'name': name, 'member': members.pack(name, h.m, h.observer, complete=rv.complete(h.m)),
         'candidates': [[cid, b.hex()] for cid, b in h.candidates],
         'observations': [b.hex() for b in env], 'checkpoint': h.checkpoint,
         'designExpect': design_expect}
    try:
        rv.replay(h, env); c['pythonOracle'] = 'accept'
    except Exception as e:
        c['pythonOracle'] = 'refuse:' + str(e)
    cases.append(c)
    rbf.create(out / (name + '.sqlite'), c)
# E1: original-only key whose retained original BLOB is empty (design: preserve
# empty original bytes as retained corrupt evidence; it is a loss, not absent).
m, o = members.build(2, 0); tcid = frame.raw_cid(b'correct'); m['objects'] = [[tcid, b'']]
h = rv.History(m, o); h.initial()
add('E1-empty-original-initial-loss', h, 'accept')
# E2: same, then a valid restoration of the correct bytes.
m, o = members.build(2, 0); tcid = frame.raw_cid(b'correct'); m['objects'] = [[tcid, b'']]
h = rv.History(m, o); h.initial(); h.restore(tcid, b'correct')
add('E2-empty-original-restored', h, 'accept')

m, o = members.build(2, 0); tcid = frame.raw_cid(b'correct'); m['objects'] = [[tcid, b'x']]
h = rv.History(m, o); h.initial(); h.restore(tcid, b'correct')
add('E3-nonempty-corrupt-original-restored-control', h, 'accept')

1	# Feature: evidence-backed conversation reconstruction
2	
3	## Summary
4	A human can open an authorized retained attempt, read its available request and
5	response, inspect normalized items against captured bytes, and see gaps and
6	unsupported formats. This versioned interpretation serves
7	`telos/raw-data-and-projections`; it never replaces the raw record or asserts
8	that a displayed speaker signed the content. This is a build contract proposal,
9	not an implemented or independently accepted capability.
10	
11	## Requirements
12	- REQ-1: Acquire every input through authorized occurrence selection and fresh source verification. Preserve snapshot, scope, occurrence, writer, proof and availability lineage; no arbitrary-CID source bypass.
13	- REQ-2: Decode bounded KANC2 frames with checked arithmetic and strict recognized shapes. Distinguish malformed, unsupported and non-capture input; account for every supplied occurrence.
14	- REQ-3: Assemble only within scope/writer/observer/attempt identity, retaining duplicates, conflicting ordinals, holes, overlaps, unknown outcomes and untrusted transport-link claims.
15	- REQ-4: Cite normalized output to exact decrypted-frame byte intervals with exclusive ends; explicitly mark enclosing/coarse spans. Do not invent precision or collapse repeated request history into new messages.
16	- REQ-5: Bound input records, source/output bytes and work. Expose partial coverage and refusal, keep integer identities exact through JavaScript, and avoid hidden whole-archive discovery.
17	- REQ-6: Version provider/harness adapters, preserve unsupported events and incomplete streaming/tool input, and distinguish protocol completeness from capture coverage. Never execute or fetch content as a side effect of rendering.
18	- REQ-7: Add human-readable Content with Source and Provenance navigation through the real API. Lock/revocation clears plaintext, selection and late responses; no persistent plaintext cache or index in this slice.
19	- REQ-8: Keep reconstruction disposable and reproducible from selected evidence plus adapter identity, preserve branches/compaction uncertainty, and qualify each substantive implementation through fresh actual Opus 5.5 review.
20	
21	## Acceptance Criteria
22	- [ ] AC-1: Byte-exact envelope fixtures reject malformed lengths, duplicate keys, body/event contradictions and unsafe integers while retaining unsupported variants visibly. (REQ-2, REQ-5)
23	- [ ] AC-2: Interleaved scopes/writers/observers, repeated identical frames, ordinal conflicts, missing chunks and contradictory end markers preserve every input lineage and explicit coverage. (REQ-1, REQ-3, REQ-8)
24	- [ ] AC-3: Independently authored fixtures verify source spans for escaped and multibyte text across capture/SSE boundaries; imprecise mappings are visibly coarse. (REQ-4, REQ-6)
25	- [ ] AC-4: Provider/harness fixtures cover tool input/result, attachments, streaming errors, unknown variants, truncated JSON, repeated history, branches and compaction without invented authorship or completeness. (REQ-3, REQ-4, REQ-6, REQ-8)
26	- [ ] AC-5: API tests reject cross-scope and revoked source selection before returning snippets/counts; cancellation and all budgets fail or report partial coverage without hidden archive scans. (REQ-1, REQ-5, REQ-7)
27	- [ ] AC-6: Real browser verification covers Content/Source/Provenance return navigation, keyboard/focus, light/dark/mobile, lock during assembly and hostile content without script execution or external requests. (REQ-4, REQ-6, REQ-7)
28	- [ ] AC-7: Reassembly after discarding derived state reproduces normalized output and citations for the same selected inputs and adapter version; unavailable inputs remain visible. (REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-8)
29	- [ ] AC-8: Fresh actual Claude Code Opus 5.5 review tests scope/identity, source lineage, limits and incomplete-coverage boundaries with independently authored probes and meaningful guard-removal controls. (REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-4, REQ-5, REQ-6, REQ-7, REQ-8)
30	
31	## Architecture
32	
33	The immutable-evidence and disposable-projection distinction follows
34	`docs/SPEC.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. The capture wire shape is implemented by
35	`src/evidence_capture.rs` (`Header`, `Event`, `Recorder::record`). Membership and
36	source verification come from `src/evidence_reader.rs`; the new explicit
37	availability boundary is `src/evidence_store/inventory.rs`. Integrate through the
38	existing frontend and reader contracts, not a second authority or a semantic
39	log rewrite. Parent scope remains `.design/kan-v2-human-frontend.md`.
40	
41	### Evidence and authorization
42	
43	All inputs enter through the configured reader, pinned inventory and fresh
44	membership checks. Parsing plaintext does not confer an archive grant. Each
45	input carries scope, selected snapshot, occurrence sequence, manifest/receipt
46	identities, authenticated writer and the available/missing/corrupt state supplied
47	by the reviewed inventory contract. An unavailable input stays a visible item.
48	The browser cannot pass an arbitrary object CID to bypass membership checks.
49	
50	Every output cites one or more input byte intervals, using exclusive ends. These
51	are offsets in decrypted retained frame bytes, not Unicode characters. If a
52	provider field cannot be mapped precisely, cite the enclosing exact JSON value
53	or entire body and label the span coarse; never invent a precise range. Escapes,
54	non-ASCII text, chunk boundaries and repeated text need independent span tests.
55	Resource links use the existing occurrence selection until a canonical URI
56	extension is reviewed. A browser fragment is not a new evidence URI scheme.
57	
58	### First adapter: the captured observation envelope
59	
60	Current recorder bytes are `KANC2`, a four-byte big-endian JSON-header length,
61	the header, then body. The writer bounds the header to 128 KiB and body to 64 KiB.
62	The decoder checks length arithmetic before allocation, UTF-8/header shape,
63	version, bounded identifiers and event/body constraints. Duplicate JSON keys
64	cannot choose different interpretations in different readers. Unknown versions
65	or event variants remain explicitly unsupported with exact source access;
66	malformed recognized envelopes are distinguished from opaque non-capture input.
67	Parsing uses no network, execution, attachment activation or persistent cache.
68	
69	Group only by `(scope, authenticated writer, observer, attempt)`. Within a group,
70	ordinal orders observations. Same-ordinal differing frames are a conflict, not
71	last-write-wins. Repeated occurrences of exact frame bytes retain all occurrence
72	lineage. A shared transport exchange is a claimed relation, not authority to
73	collapse observers or writers into one sequence. Wall-clock time never repairs
74	missing order or proves causal linkage.
75	
76	Request/response offsets determine byte assembly. Holes, overlaps, contradictory
77	end counts, missing initial events and truncated selections remain visible.
78	`unconfirmed_before` is an observer claim, not an exact count of lost remote
79	records. RequestEnd may establish the recorded request byte extent when all
80	segments agree. A completed terminal observation does not establish complete
81	traffic capture. Missing terminal observations display outcome unknown.
82	
83	Assembly has explicit input-record, source-byte, output-byte and time budgets;
84	limits return partial coverage and continuation or a refusal, never empty success.
85	No request silently scans the whole archive to find an attempt. The first API
86	accepts a bounded authorized occurrence selection; broader discovery requires
87	the later indexed selection contract. All u64 coordinates cross JavaScript as
88	validated decimal strings or checked safe integers, never rounded identifiers.
89	
90	### Provider and harness adapters
91	
92	Adapters have explicit name/version and report supported event forms. The first
93	provider adapter targets the existing Anthropic harness profile. Protocol
94	references were checked on 2026-10-19; supported forms remain versioned, not
95	inferred from a provider name alone. It must handle streamed event
96	boundaries independently of capture chunks, incomplete SSE events, tool inputs
97	and results, text blocks, attachments, errors and unknown variants. Each new
98	provider is a separate reviewed adapter with preserved raw fixtures.
99	
100	A request often repeats earlier conversation history. It is not a new occurrence
101	of every historical message. Cross-request sessions require explicit evidence
102	links and a declared reconstruction rule; matching content or timestamps alone
103	cannot invent identity. Branches and compaction retain their source relationships
104	and ambiguity. Tool labels are provider/harness claims, not cryptographic authors.
105	Unknown attachment bytes remain inspectable/downloadable under existing grants;
106	no external URL is fetched just because it appears in a message.
107	
108	### Human workflow
109	
110	The Library adds Content beside Source and Provenance. Attempt view shows ordered
111	observations, request/response reading panes, gaps/conflicts and adapter coverage.
112	Selecting a rendered item selects its source intervals. Unsupported content
113	always retains a path to authorized raw inspection. Session navigation appears
114	only when that real API is integrated; it is not enabled by a synthetic mock.
115	
116	Lock and access revocation invalidate assembly, selections and late responses in
117	the same way as source reads. Responses are no-store. No decrypted reconstruction
118	is persisted in browser storage, temporary files, logs or a server index in this
119	slice. Persistent search comes later with encrypted projection and revocation
120	contracts; that remains required by the full frontend, not removed from scope.
121	
122	
123	### Primary protocol grounding
124	
125	The provider adapter follows message and indexed-content-block boundaries,
126	retains ping/error/unknown events, and handles text, tool-input and thinking
127	variants separately. Transport chunks are not provider event boundaries.
128	See [Anthropic streaming messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming).
129	
130	Tool-input fragments may remain invalid JSON even when streaming ends; the
131	initial empty input object is a placeholder. Concatenate bounded fragments,
132	guard parsing and retain truncated input as an explicit partial item. Do not
133	repair it silently or run the tool.
134	See [Anthropic fine-grained tool streaming](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/fine-grained-tool-streaming).
135	
136	These are protocol inputs to a Kan interpretation, not promises that every
137	existing provider extension is supported. Fixtures must name their adapter
138	version and cover unknown variants. Recheck primary docs when implementing a
139	new adapter rather than updating old derived records in place.
140	
141	## Sequencing and remaining scope
142	
143	First qualify the pure envelope decoder and occurrence assembly using synthetic
144	fixtures. Then qualify the initial provider adapter and source spans, followed
145	by authorized API integration and real browser behavior. Storage inventory and
146	recovery integration remain separate prerequisites to browsing damaged archives.
147	Search, annotations, saved views, background extraction/day assessment and full
148	administration remain required by the overall frontend roadmap. None is closed
149	by this document or the first Content panel.
150	
151	## Recording and validation status
152	
153	This continues the existing local draft; no new product decision is required.
154	Git-first recording remains necessary while worktree day/kan discovery refuses
155	shared repository state (day#168/kan#197). Do not reconstruct the two withheld
156	claims or invent witnesses for the existing telos. Design recording and bridge
157	claims require later backfill; no claim CIDs or witnessed completion are asserted.
158	Run the actual design validator and preserve its output, including any root-
159	checkout path warnings, separately from implementation acceptance.
160	
161	## First implementation checkpoint: pure frame decoder
162	
163	`src/evidence_reconstruction.rs` adds a bounded, non-persistent decoder only.
164	It returns opaque, unsupported, malformed or recognized capture input separately.
165	The recognized frame exposes borrowed body bytes and exact header/body ranges;
166	it has no wire serializer, grant, signature judgment or assembly-completeness
167	claim. JSON maps reject duplicate keys recursively, including escaped aliases,
168	before variant selection. Unknown envelope/version/observer/event/outcome is
169	unsupported; unsupported means no semantic fields are accepted, not that all
170	remaining fields satisfy a known schema. Recognized shapes use the current
171	strict capture Header/Event types and recorder byte/identifier limits.
172	
173	HTTP directions, offsets, totals, status and timestamps remain observer claims;
174	coherence belongs to later assembly. This checkpoint does not silently tighten
175	the recorder's historical semantic guarantees. KANC-family truncation beginning
176	with the four-byte family prefix is malformed; inputs without that prefix are
177	opaque. Decode requires a complete retained frame, not a source-range fragment.
178	All storage/RPC/browser/session acceptance remains open. No persistence surface
179	is added by this pure function.
180	
181	### Decoder review decisions
182	
183	The first independent decoder review found that Serde's internally tagged unit
184	variant silently ignores extra fields. Forwarding-intent now explicitly refuses
185	anything beyond its type field; every recognized event has an extra-field test.
186	A recognized header must include `observed_at_unix_micros`: explicit null retains
187	the recorder's unavailable-clock claim, whereas absence is malformed. Unknown
188	variants still accept no semantic interpretation. Noncanonical JSON whitespace
189	and escaping remain accepted when unambiguous; exact original spans are retained.
190	
191	For every input beginning `KANC`, the total-frame size limit precedes envelope
192	version classification, including unknown envelope versions. Thus oversized
193	unknown KANC-family data is a limit refusal. Inputs without the KANC prefix remain
194	opaque without parsing or copying, regardless of size. Downstream source-read
195	budgets remain responsible for all input acquisition. These choices do not
196	assert coverage or close the parent reconstruction acceptance criteria.
197	
198	The second cold review's PA1/PA2 probes are promoted into the normal test suite:
199	accepted recognized frames must round-trip to the parsed JSON value across the
200	mutation corpus, and absent clocks on unknown versions/observers/events/outcomes
201	remain Unsupported. This pins classification precedence and catches future
202	optional-field or unit-variant narrowing before a consumer is added.
203	
204	## Next implementation checkpoint: bounded occurrence assembly

and results, text blocks, attachments, errors and unknown variants. Each new
provider is a separate reviewed adapter with preserved raw fixtures.

A request often repeats earlier conversation history. It is not a new occurrence
of every historical message. Cross-request sessions require explicit evidence
links and a declared reconstruction rule; matching content or timestamps alone
cannot invent identity. Branches and compaction retain their source relationships
and ambiguity. Tool labels are provider/harness claims, not cryptographic authors.
Unknown attachment bytes remain inspectable/downloadable under existing grants;
no external URL is fetched just because it appears in a message.

### Human workflow

The Library adds Content beside Source and Provenance. Attempt view shows ordered
observations, request/response reading panes, gaps/conflicts and adapter coverage.
Selecting a rendered item selects its source intervals. Unsupported content
always retains a path to authorized raw inspection. Session navigation appears
only when that real API is integrated; it is not enabled by a synthetic mock.

Lock and access revocation invalidate assembly, selections and late responses in
the same way as source reads. Responses are no-store. No decrypted reconstruction
is persisted in browser storage, temporary files, logs or a server index in this
slice. Persistent search comes later with encrypted projection and revocation
contracts; that remains required by the full frontend, not removed from scope.


### Primary protocol grounding

The provider adapter follows message and indexed-content-block boundaries,
retains ping/error/unknown events, and handles text, tool-input and thinking
variants separately. Transport chunks are not provider event boundaries.
See [Anthropic streaming messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming).

Tool-input fragments may remain invalid JSON even when streaming ends; the
initial empty input object is a placeholder. Concatenate bounded fragments,
guard parsing and retain truncated input as an explicit partial item. Do not
repair it silently or run the tool.
See [Anthropic fine-grained tool streaming](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/fine-grained-tool-streaming).

These are protocol inputs to a Kan interpretation, not promises that every
existing provider extension is supported. Fixtures must name their adapter
version and cover unknown variants. Recheck primary docs when implementing a
new adapter rather than updating old derived records in place.

## Sequencing and remaining scope

First qualify the pure envelope decoder and occurrence assembly using synthetic
fixtures. Then qualify the initial provider adapter and source spans, followed
by authorized API integration and real browser behavior. Storage inventory and
recovery integration remain separate prerequisites to browsing damaged archives.
Search, annotations, saved views, background extraction/day assessment and full
administration remain required by the overall frontend roadmap. None is closed
by this document or the first Content panel.

## Recording and validation status

This continues the existing local draft; no new product decision is required.
Git-first recording remains necessary while worktree day/kan discovery refuses
shared repository state (day#168/kan#197). Do not reconstruct the two withheld
claims or invent witnesses for the existing telos. Design recording and bridge
claims require later backfill; no claim CIDs or witnessed completion are asserted.
Run the actual design validator and preserve its output, including any root-
checkout path warnings, separately from implementation acceptance.

## First implementation checkpoint: pure frame decoder

`src/evidence_reconstruction.rs` adds a bounded, non-persistent decoder only.
It returns opaque, unsupported, malformed or recognized capture input separately.
The recognized frame exposes borrowed body bytes and exact header/body ranges;
it has no wire serializer, grant, signature judgment or assembly-completeness
claim. JSON maps reject duplicate keys recursively, including escaped aliases,
before variant selection. Unknown envelope/version/observer/event/outcome is
unsupported; unsupported means no semantic fields are accepted, not that all
remaining fields satisfy a known schema. Recognized shapes use the current
strict capture Header/Event types and recorder byte/identifier limits.

HTTP directions, offsets, totals, status and timestamps remain observer claims;
coherence belongs to later assembly. This checkpoint does not silently tighten
the recorder's historical semantic guarantees. KANC-family truncation beginning
with the four-byte family prefix is malformed; inputs without that prefix are
opaque. Decode requires a complete retained frame, not a source-range fragment.
All storage/RPC/browser/session acceptance remains open. No persistence surface
is added by this pure function.

### Decoder review decisions

The first independent decoder review found that Serde's internally tagged unit
variant silently ignores extra fields. Forwarding-intent now explicitly refuses
anything beyond its type field; every recognized event has an extra-field test.
A recognized header must include `observed_at_unix_micros`: explicit null retains
the recorder's unavailable-clock claim, whereas absence is malformed. Unknown
variants still accept no semantic interpretation. Noncanonical JSON whitespace
and escaping remain accepted when unambiguous; exact original spans are retained.

For every input beginning `KANC`, the total-frame size limit precedes envelope
version classification, including unknown envelope versions. Thus oversized
unknown KANC-family data is a limit refusal. Inputs without the KANC prefix remain
opaque without parsing or copying, regardless of size. Downstream source-read
budgets remain responsible for all input acquisition. These choices do not
assert coverage or close the parent reconstruction acceptance criteria.

The second cold review's PA1/PA2 probes are promoted into the normal test suite:
accepted recognized frames must round-trip to the parsed JSON value across the
mutation corpus, and absent clocks on unknown versions/observers/events/outcomes
remain Unsupported. This pins classification precedence and catches future
optional-field or unit-variant narrowing before a consumer is added.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Selected compiled assembly controls; each restores exact source bytes."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SOURCE=ROOT/'src/evidence_assembly.rs'
BASE=ROOT/'.local-state/assembly-author'
OUT=BASE/('controls-'+str(len(list(BASE.glob('controls-*')))+1))
ISOLATION='scope_writer_observer_attempt_isolation_ignores_transport_link_claims'
CASES=[
 ('scope-key','inputs[i].scope,','[0;32],',ISOLATION),
 ('writer-key','inputs[i].writer,','"ignored-writer",',ISOLATION),
 ('observer-key','                    observer,','                    0,',ISOLATION),
 ('attempt-key','&f.header.attempt,','"ignored-attempt",',ISOLATION),
 ('duplicate-conflict','                    conflict = true;','                    conflict = false;','ordinal_conflicts_keep_both_bytes_and_prevent_synthetic_rendering'),
 ('gap-rendering','if out.issues.is_empty()','if true || out.issues.is_empty()','holes_overlaps_and_contradictory_extents_are_not_repaired'),
 ('assembled-budget','self.assembled > self.limits.assembled_bytes','false && self.assembled > self.limits.assembled_bytes','exact_budget_edges_cancellation_and_repeat_are_deterministic'),
 ('source-lineage','sources: sources\n','sources: sources[..1]\n','shuffled_selection_preserves_exact_binary_spans_and_duplicate_lineage'),
]
def main():
 if not __debug__:raise RuntimeError('assertions required')
 original=SOURCE.read_text();OUT.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
 try:
  for name,old,new,test in CASES:
   assert original.count(old)==1,(name,original.count(old))
   SOURCE.write_text(original.replace(old,new))
   r=subprocess.run(['cargo','test','--features','v2-crypto','--test','evidence_assembly',test,'--','--exact','--nocapture'],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=240)
   log=r.stdout+r.stderr; (OUT/(name+'.txt')).write_text(log+'\nexit='+str(r.returncode)+'\n')
   assert r.returncode and 'could not compile' not in log,name+' survived or did not compile'
   assert 'test '+test+' ... FAILED' in log,name+' lacks named assertion failure'
   assert ('assertion' in log or (name == 'assembled-budget' and 'called `Result::unwrap_err()` on an `Ok` value: Assembly' in log)),name+' lacks semantic assertion'
   print('DEMONSTRATED: '+name,flush=True)
 finally:SOURCE.write_text(original)
 r=subprocess.run(['cargo','test','--features','v2-crypto','--test','evidence_assembly'],cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=240)
 (OUT/'restored.txt').write_text(r.stdout+r.stderr+'\nexit='+str(r.returncode)+'\n');assert r.returncode==0
 print('Eight selected controls demonstrated; restored assembly tests pass.',flush=True)
if __name__=='__main__':main()

# Session assembly author qualification

Thirty integration tests (13 assembly, 15 decoder, two decoder review regressions)
and one deterministic mid-decode cancellation unit pass. Strict all-target v2
Clippy and formatting pass. Initial formatting failure is retained.

Eight selected compiled controls demonstrate scope/writer/observer/attempt
isolation, ordinal conflict handling, gap refusal, assembled-byte budget and
complete duplicate lineage. Restored 13-test assembly suite passes. The first
control run incorrectly required the literal word assertion: the budget mutant
correctly failed unwrap_err on an unexpected successful Assembly. That complete
failed run is retained; the harness now recognizes this exact semantic failure
for that control. No production code changed to satisfy the harness.

Initial PR CI had 20 successful checks and one context scaling failure (ratio
8.4 against bound 8). The default-feature measured binary excludes the new
v2-crypto module; Cargo manifests/lock and performance paths are unchanged.
The raw failure is retained and a single failed-job rerun was requested. This
is unresolved CI evidence, not a claimed pass or proof of noise.

Day validation refuses the worktree with exit 2 under day#168/kan#197, not a
passing check. No main-workspace log write occurred. Fresh actual Opus review
remains required. No session API, provider adapter or frontend integration is
claimed, and no parent frontend acceptance criterion closes here.

"""Python SQLite physical fixtures carrying independently signed replay vectors.

The existing proposed DDL fixture pins the schema; it is not an independently
designed schema specification. Byte/signature/state authority comes from the independent
replay vectors. No Rust invocation, production keys or network.
"""
import argparse,json,os,sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

def create(path,case,encoding='UTF-8'):
    schema=(ROOT/'.design/fixtures/recovery-bundle-v1-schema.sql').read_text()
    fd=os.open(path,os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL,0o600);os.close(fd)
    db=sqlite3.connect(path)
    db.execute("PRAGMA encoding='"+encoding+"'")
    db.executescript(schema)
    db.execute('PRAGMA application_id=1263419953')
    assert 1263419953==0x4b4e4231
    db.execute('PRAGMA user_version=1')
    # Hostile vectors can contain states that storage constraints alone refuse.
    # Disable CHECK constraints for fixture insertion to exercise reader checks.
    db.execute('PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints=ON')
    m=case['member'];c=m['context'];unhex=bytes.fromhex
    db.execute('INSERT INTO bundle_identity VALUES(1,?,?,?,?,?,?)',(unhex(c['bundle']),c['observer'],c['profile'],unhex(c['archive']),unhex(c['scope']),c['issuer']))
    if m['plan'] is not None:db.execute('INSERT INTO member_plan VALUES(1,?)',(unhex(m['plan']),))
    db.executemany('INSERT INTO member_membership VALUES(?,?)',m['membership'])
    db.executemany('INSERT INTO member_records VALUES(?,?,?,?)',[(n,unhex(a),unhex(b),unhex(c)) for n,a,b,c in m['records']])
    db.executemany('INSERT INTO member_objects VALUES(?,?)',[(c,unhex(b)) for c,b in m['objects']])
    db.executemany('INSERT INTO restored_objects VALUES(?,?)',[(c,unhex(b)) for c,b in case['candidates']])
    db.executemany('INSERT INTO observations VALUES(?,?)',[(i+1,unhex(b)) for i,b in enumerate(case['observations'])])
    db.commit();db.close()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reviewer scope-A probe generator (not the author's selection).
Signed histories use the repo's public test-key primitives (recovery_replay_vectors);
physical files use the author's fixture constructor, then reviewer SQL mutations.
Expectations are written from the design text before running Rust:
  - empty original BLOB = retained corrupt evidence (a loss), must be accepted
  - source TEXT / empty candidate must still refuse.
Usage: gen_A_probes.py OUT_DIR EXPORT_DIR
"""
import json, sys, sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
out = Path(sys.argv[1]); EXPORT = Path(sys.argv[2])
sys.path.insert(0, str(EXPORT / '.design/tools'))
import recovery_replay_vectors as rv
import recovery_bundle_files as rbf
members, frame = rv.members, rv.frame
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
cases = []

def add(name, m, observer, restores, expect, sql=None, expect_err=None):
    h = rv.History(m, observer); h.initial()
    for cid, data in restores:
        h.restore(cid, data)
    env = h.encoded()
    c = {'name': name, 'member': members.pack(name, m, observer, complete=rv.complete(m)),
         'candidates': [[cid, b.hex()] for cid, b in h.candidates],
         'observations': [b.hex() for b in env], 'checkpoint': h.checkpoint,
         'designExpect': expect, 'expectErr': expect_err, 'sql': sql,
         'emptyOriginals': [cid for cid, b in m['objects'] if b == b'']}
    try:
        rv.replay(h, env); c['pythonOracle'] = 'accept'
    except Exception as e:
        c['pythonOracle'] = 'refuse:' + str(e)
    path = out / (name + '.sqlite')
    rbf.create(path, c)
    if sql:
        db = sqlite3.connect(path)
        db.execute('PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints=ON')
        cur = db.execute(sql)
        c['sqlChanged'] = cur.rowcount
        db.commit(); db.close()
    cases.append(c)

# PA1/PA2: COMPLETE profile 3 (not covered by author's E4/E5 partial cases).
def p3_complete():
    m, o = members.build(3, 3)
    cid, correct = m['objects'][0]
    m['objects'][0] = [cid, b'']
    return m, o, cid, correct
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
add('PA1-p3-complete-empty-original-initial-loss', m, o, [], 'accept')
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
add('PA2-p3-complete-empty-original-restored', m, o, [(cid, correct)], 'accept')
# PA3: partial profile 3, TWO empty originals, only one restored.
m, o = members.build(3, 3); m['records'] = m['records'][:1]
(c0, k0), (c1, k1) = m['objects'][0], m['objects'][1]
m['objects'][0] = [c0, b'']; m['objects'][1] = [c1, b'']
add('PA3-p3-partial-two-empty-one-restored', m, o, [(c0, k0)], 'accept')
# PA4: profile 2, two original-only keys, both empty, both restored.
m, o = members.build(2, 0)
ca, cb = frame.raw_cid(b'alpha'), frame.raw_cid(b'beta')
m['objects'] = sorted([[ca, b''], [cb, b'']])
add('PA4-p2-two-empty-both-restored', m, o, sorted([(ca, b'alpha'), (cb, b'beta')]), 'accept')
# Hostile physical mutations of otherwise-accepted histories.
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
add('PH1-empty-original-stored-as-TEXT', m, o, [], 'refuse',
    "UPDATE member_objects SET bytes=CAST(x'' AS TEXT) WHERE length(bytes)=0", 'cell storage class')
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
add('PH2-empty-candidate-blob', m, o, [(cid, correct)], 'refuse',
    "UPDATE restored_objects SET bytes=x''", 'integer storage class or bounds')
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
add('PH3-empty-candidate-TEXT', m, o, [(cid, correct)], 'refuse',
    "UPDATE restored_objects SET bytes=CAST(x'' AS TEXT)", 'cell storage class')
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
add('PH4-empty-original-rewritten-as-zeroblob0', m, o, [], 'accept',
    "UPDATE member_objects SET bytes=zeroblob(0) WHERE length(bytes)=0")
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
# A nonempty original made empty AFTER signing: the history committed to the
# nonempty object, so the physical file no longer matches -> must refuse (not
# be smoothed over by the empty-projection admission).
add('PH5-nonempty-original-truncated-to-empty-after-signing', m, o, [], 'refuse',
    "UPDATE member_objects SET bytes=x'' WHERE length(bytes)>0 AND cid=(SELECT min(cid) FROM member_objects WHERE length(bytes)>0)", None)
m, o, cid, correct = p3_complete()
# Retained empty original replaced by a NUL byte (1 byte) after signing -> refuse.
add('PH6-empty-original-replaced-by-one-byte', m, o, [], 'refuse',
    "UPDATE member_objects SET bytes=x'00' WHERE length(bytes)=0", None)
(out / 'cases.json').write_text(json.dumps({'cases': cases}, indent=1))
for c in cases:
    print(c['name'], 'designExpect=' + c['designExpect'], 'pythonOracle(pre-mutation history)=' + c['pythonOracle'],
          'sqlChanged=' + str(c.get('sqlChanged')), 'emptyOriginals=%d' % len(c['emptyOriginals']))

Expectations are written from the design text before running Rust:

import recovery_bundle_files as rbf
members, frame = rv.members, rv.frame
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
cases = []

    h = rv.History(m, observer); h.initial()
    for cid, data in restores:
        h.restore(cid, data)
    env = h.encoded()
    c = {'name': name, 'member': members.pack(name, m, observer, complete=rv.complete(m)),
         'candidates': [[cid, b.hex()] for cid, b in h.candidates],

         'emptyOriginals': [cid for cid, b in m['objects'] if b == b'']}

    rbf.create(path, c)
    if sql:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reviewer mutation driver. One mutant at a time; exact pinned SHA-256 restore after each.
Usage: mutate.py SPEC_JSON   where SPEC is a list of
  {"id","file","old","new","runs":[[test_target, filter_or_null, extra_env_or_null]], "expect"}
A mutant is KILLED only if it compiles and some named test FAILS. Compile failure is reported
as COMPILE-FAIL (not a kill). Raw output per mutant goes to review-evidence/mutations/<id>.txt.
"""
import hashlib, json, os, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
EXPORT = Path('/Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-session-assembly/.local-state/reviews/assembly-opening')
ident = json.load(open(EXPORT.parent / 'assembly-opening-identity.json'))
OUT = EXPORT / 'review-evidence/mutations'; OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
spec = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
summary = []
for m in spec:
    path = EXPORT / m['file']
    orig = path.read_bytes()
    assert hashlib.sha256(orig).hexdigest() == ident['files'][m['file']], 'pre-state not pinned: ' + m['file']
    text = orig.decode()
    count = text.count(m['old'])
    log = [f"# {m['id']}: {m['file']}\n# expect: {m['expect']}\n# old occurrences={count}\n--- old\n{m['old']}\n+++ new\n{m['new']}\n"]
    verdict = None
    if count != 1:
        verdict = 'NOT-APPLIED(count=%d)' % count
    else:
        try:
            path.write_text(text.replace(m['old'], m['new']))
            failed, compiled = [], True
            for target, filt, env in m['runs']:
                args = ['cargo', 'test', '--features', 'v2-crypto', '--test', target]
                if filt: args += [filt]
                args += ['--', '--nocapture']
                e = dict(os.environ); e.update(env or {})
                r = subprocess.run(args, cwd=EXPORT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900, env=e)
                out = r.stdout + r.stderr
                log.append('$ ' + ' '.join(args) + f"  env={env}\n" + out + f'\nexit={r.returncode}\n')
                if 'could not compile' in out or 'error[E' in out:
                    compiled = False
                failed += [l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith('test ') and l.endswith('FAILED')]
            verdict = 'COMPILE-FAIL' if not compiled else ('KILLED by ' + '; '.join(failed) if failed else 'SURVIVED')
        finally:
            path.write_bytes(orig)
    ok = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == ident['files'][m['file']]
    log.append(f'\nVERDICT {verdict}\nrestored_exact={ok}\n')
    (OUT / (m['id'] + '.txt')).write_text('\n'.join(log))
    summary.append(f"{m['id']}: {verdict} | restored_exact={ok} | expect: {m['expect']}")
    print(summary[-1], flush=True)
    assert ok
(OUT / ('driver-' + Path(sys.argv[1]).stem + '.txt')).write_text('\n'.join(summary) + '\n')

# Feature: create and restore retained recovery bundles

## Summary
Continue the approved KNB1 design with owner-side physical creation and restoration. A stopped or pinned profile-2/3 source becomes a new retained bundle; restoration appends verified ciphertext and its signed observation together. The original source, member evidence and previous observations remain unchanged. This is a dependent implementation plan, pending the physical-reader review; it does not report these APIs as implemented.

## Requirements
- REQ-1: Before opening any SQLite participant, check source and destination main/sidecar custody and collisions using the existing evidence-store conventions. Creation exclusively reserves a new private file; neither retry nor error overwrites an existing output.
- REQ-2: Acquire the exact canonical metadata, proof bytes, original plan/membership and every bounded original object from one source snapshot. Validate independently supplied archive/scope/issuer/profile and selected metadata frontier. Ignore repairable derived columns, but refuse unknown schema, malformed physical types, extra proof coordinates, noncanonical keys and oversized cells without silently omitting them.
- REQ-3: Construct the created event and exact initial loss partition from the verified member. Commit the complete member, history and KNB1 markers together, then synchronize the file and parent and independently reopen before returning success.
- REQ-4: Restoration requires the owner-pinned observer and exact latest checkpoint under a write transaction. Verify candidate membership, length, CID, and referenced writer signature/binding before signing. Append candidate and observation atomically; never modify original rows or old observations. An exact repeat is idempotent and reports its original observation without appending another.
- REQ-5: Enforce explicit acquisition, semantic-work, item, time/cancellation and output-size limits. Limits do not introduce a universal archive-size ceiling. Preserve failed output artifacts and distinguish pre-commit refusal from an outcome uncertain after commit.
- REQ-6: Extend typed mutation capabilities and the independent persistence catalog with the implementation. Exercise abrupt process death, source invariance, stale checkpoint/concurrent writers, invalid candidates and standalone refusal, and obtain fresh actual Opus review.

# Feature: Kan Studio — the complete human frontend

## Summary
Build a full human client for Kan: a rich, navigable library of retained work, messages, evidence, annotations and interpretations, with process assessment and administration in the same coherent application. Operations is one area, not the product boundary. Use the user's selected technical-studio direction: clean light surfaces, dense data and vivid accents.

This design supersedes the initial operations-only choice following the user's explicit clarification. It preserves `.design/kan-v2-server-first.md`: centralized cross-project evidence, blind storage, separately authorized readers, provenance-preserving projections, explicit missing evidence and eventual day integration. The companion `.design/kan-v2-operations-polish.md` covers every operations review follow-up. This design does not claim the full frontend or its missing backend contracts are implemented.

## Requirements
- REQ-1: Provide coherent navigation across Library, Sessions, Knowledge, Saved views, Analysis, Operations, Storage/recovery, Migration and Access/settings. A complete frontend includes readable evidence and useful human workflows, not just admin metrics.
- REQ-2: Browse and search authorized retained data across projects, scopes, hosts, observers, time, type and tags, with bounded pagination and stable deep links. Project grouping never implies scope access. Show selection, source/index frontier, exclusions and incomplete coverage.
- REQ-3: Read reconstructed sessions with user/assistant/tool events, attachments, branches, compaction and gaps; inspect the exact captured source alongside each normalized rendering. Unsupported payloads remain downloadable/inspectable subject to grants and size limits, not silently omitted.
- REQ-4: Distinguish raw observed evidence, human annotations, imported v1 claims and model-produced interpretations. Inspect origin, observer, claimed speaker, signature validity, scope admission, consumer trust and citations separately. Every derived summary can lead back to exact source spans and the run that produced it.
- REQ-5: Create explicit attributed annotations, tags, relations and saved views through the shared signed/encrypted API. Edits append new records and preserve prior history; retraction does not destroy a subject. Preview scope, target and effect before committing a user action.
- REQ-6: Make views first-class, with selectable authorized scopes, snapshot/frontier, trust/enrichment frame, filters and grouping. Offer table, session and relation views with textual equivalents. Contradictory witnesses remain accessible; no similarity/cluster result silently creates identity.
- REQ-7: Expose background extraction and day-style assessment as inspectable jobs/runs: input selection, recipe/prompt/schema, model identity, trigger, progress, attempts, outputs, cost when available and exact evidence lineage. Explicit user actions can schedule work under grants/quotas; viewing content cannot execute instructions found in it.
- REQ-8: Include the complete operational/admin surface: capture sources, spool/ledger health, retained gaps, journal rotation, backup checkpoints, restore verification, migration inventory/plans/progress, scope memberships, reader/writer grants, key epochs and instance configuration. Owners must be able to execute supported administrative tasks from the full frontend through separately authorized plan/job APIs, including rotation; permanent CLI-only instructions do not satisfy full-frontend completion. Read capability, mutation capability and missing backend support are explicit.
- REQ-9: Keep blind storage separate from the plaintext reader/index and optional annotation signer. A browser session gets only authorized data and operations; neither an operations token nor an ordinary reader session gains archive-admin or signing authority implicitly. Secret key material never enters view URLs, diagnostics or ordinary browser persistence.
- REQ-10: Treat captured content as untrusted. Render text/Markdown/code without executable HTML, script, external resource loading or active attachments; expose safe source views and explicit downloads. Search, snippets, facets, counts, exports and derived results obey scope authorization without existence leaks.
- REQ-11: Deliver accessible, responsive, polished human interaction: keyboard navigation, visible focus, usable long documents/tables, error/loading/empty/locked states, inspector focus management, reduced motion and text-labeled status. Avoid invented data visualizations or dead navigation masquerading as implemented functionality.
- REQ-12: Track end-to-end feature completeness through a capability matrix and reviewed vertical slices. Preserve CLI/MCP/API semantics and canonical identity/URI rules; every new writer extends persistence conformance. No phase is called a complete frontend until its human workflows work against real APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-1: From the real Library, find a retained session across two authorized projects, narrow by observer/time/tag, paginate at a pinned snapshot, open a stable link and return to the same list state. An unauthorized third scope contributes no snippets, facet counts or inferred existence. Missing/stale indexes produce incomplete coverage, not empty success. (REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-9, REQ-10)
- [ ] AC-2: A fixture session containing tool output, an attachment, branches, compaction, cancellation and an unknown payload type renders every available event or a typed unavailable state. Source inspection/export reproduces exact selected retained bytes; normalized speaker labels never imply a signature that does not exist. (REQ-3, REQ-4)
- [ ] AC-3: Follow a summary to its extraction run, input manifest and cited byte/span references; compare two conflicting interpretations without overwriting either. Inspect imported v1 origin and all four read judgments. Broken, withheld and erased references retain distinct authorized states. (REQ-4, REQ-7)
- [ ] AC-4: Annotate a selected source span, preview scope/author/effect, submit with an idempotency key, lose the response and retry without duplicate attribution. Edit/retract while preserving history and provenance. The same operation through CLI and UI yields equivalent signed/encrypted records. (REQ-5, REQ-9, REQ-12)
- [ ] AC-5: Save a view with a pinned input/trust frame; reopening it produces the same membership and judgments despite arrival-order changes. Changing trust or scope produces a visibly different view. Relation inspection retains witnesses and contradictory paths; accessible list/table views expose the same relationships. (REQ-6)
- [ ] AC-6: Schedule an authorized analysis over an explicit selection, inspect its plan, interrupt/retry, and retain every attempt plus unknown provider outcomes. A changed recipe creates a new run; a captured prompt-injection string cannot grant access or schedule work. Unsupported costs/versions are unknown, not zero or invented. (REQ-7, REQ-9, REQ-10)
- [ ] AC-7: Exercise the operations state matrix and all rotation/recovery controls in the companion design. From the human UI inspect a backup checkpoint, a restore verification report, a migration plan with per-source failures and the final-delta/cutover preconditions. Mutation actions require their own capability and a concrete preview. Execute an owner-authorized synthetic rotation through the admin API, observe progress/reconnect, and compare its effects to the CLI protocol; a read-only operations token must be denied. Synthetic fixtures only until deployment is separately authorized. (REQ-8)
- [ ] AC-8: Revoke reader access and verify subsequent reads, indexes, snippets, attachments and exports cannot disclose the revoked scope. Lock clears rendered content and client query caches; responses are no-store. Verify CSRF/origin/session boundaries on mutations and prevent admin or signer privilege through a read-only session. Revocation makes no promise to recall plaintext already copied by a user. (REQ-9, REQ-10)
- [ ] AC-9: Browser tests at desktop, tablet and 390px cover all implemented navigation, filters, keyboard interactions, long identifiers, large paginated lists, inspector open/close, failed fetch, empty/partial results and lock. No body-level horizontal overflow; raw tables may scroll within labeled regions. No external asset requests or executable captured content. (REQ-11)
- [ ] AC-10: Each screen's capability matrix names real API contracts, tests and exact reviewed commits. A UI-only mock or CLI primitive is not marked integrated. Fresh actual Claude Code Opus 5.5 reviews substantive builds/fix rounds; finding fixes include whole-production-fix reversion evidence. (REQ-12)

## Architecture

### Human information architecture

| Area | Human task | Detail/secondary views |
|---|---|---|
| Library | Find anything retained or derived within authorized inputs | Global search, facets, result type, source preview, coverage, export selection |

Inspect origin, observer, claimed speaker, signature validity, scope admission, consumer trust and citations separately. Every derived summary can lead back to exact source spans and the run that produced it.
- REQ-5: Create explicit attributed annotations, tags, relations and saved views through the shared signed/encrypted API. Edits append new records and preserve prior history; retraction does not destroy a subject. Preview scope, target and effect before committing a user action.
- REQ-6: Make views first-class, with selectable authorized scopes, snapshot/frontier, trust/enrichment frame, filters and grouping. Offer table, session and relation views with textual equivalents. Contradictory witnesses remain accessible; no similarity/cluster result silently creates identity.
- REQ-7: Expose background extraction and day-style assessment as inspectable jobs/runs: input selection, recipe/prompt/schema, model identity, trigger, progress, attempts, outputs, cost when available and exact evidence lineage. Explicit user actions can schedule work under grants/quotas; viewing content cannot execute instructions found in it.
- REQ-8: Include the complete operational/admin surface: capture sources, spool/ledger health, retained gaps, journal rotation, backup checkpoints, restore verification, migration inventory/plans/progress, scope memberships, reader/writer grants, key epochs and instance configuration. Owners must be able to execute supported administrative tasks from the full frontend through separately authorized plan/job APIs, including rotation; permanent CLI-only instructions do not satisfy full-frontend completion. Read capability, mutation capability and missing backend support are explicit.
- REQ-9: Keep blind storage separate from the plaintext reader/index and optional annotation signer. A browser session gets only authorized data and operations; neither an operations token nor an ordinary reader session gains archive-admin or signing authority implicitly. Secret key material never enters view URLs, diagnostics or ordinary browser persistence.
- REQ-10: Treat captured content as untrusted. Render text/Markdown/code without executable HTML, script, external resource loading or active attachments; expose safe source views and explicit downloads. Search, snippets, facets, counts, exports and derived results obey scope authorization without existence leaks.
- REQ-11: Deliver accessible, responsive, polished human interaction: keyboard navigation, visible focus, usable long documents/tables, error/loading/empty/locked states, inspector focus management, reduced motion and text-labeled status. Avoid invented data visualizations or dead navigation masquerading as implemented functionality.
- REQ-12: Track end-to-end feature completeness through a capability matrix and reviewed vertical slices. Preserve CLI/MCP/API semantics and canonical identity/URI rules; every new writer extends persistence conformance. No phase is called a complete frontend until its human workflows work against real APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-1: From the real Library, find a retained session across two authorized projects, narrow by observer/time/tag, paginate at a pinned snapshot, open a stable link and return to the same list state. An unauthorized third scope contributes no snippets, facet counts or inferred existence. Missing/stale indexes produce incomplete coverage, not empty success. (REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-9, REQ-10)
- [ ] AC-2: A fixture session containing tool output, an attachment, branches, compaction, cancellation and an unknown payload type renders every available event or a typed unavailable state. Source inspection/export reproduces exact selected retained bytes; normalized speaker labels never imply a signature that does not exist. (REQ-3, REQ-4)
- [ ] AC-3: Follow a summary to its extraction run, input manifest and cited byte/span references; compare two conflicting interpretations without overwriting either. Inspect imported v1 origin and all four read judgments. Broken, withheld and erased references retain distinct authorized states. (REQ-4, REQ-7)
- [ ] AC-4: Annotate a selected source span, preview scope/author/effect, submit with an idempotency key, lose the response and retry without duplicate attribution. Edit/retract while preserving history and provenance. The same operation through CLI and UI yields equivalent signed/encrypted records. (REQ-5, REQ-9, REQ-12)
- [ ] AC-5: Save a view with a pinned input/trust frame; reopening it produces the same membership and judgments despite arrival-order changes. Changing trust or scope produces a visibly different view. Relation inspection retains witnesses and contradictory paths; accessible list/table views expose the same relationships. (REQ-6)
- [ ] AC-6: Schedule an authorized analysis over an explicit selection, inspect its plan, interrupt/retry, and retain every attempt plus unknown provider outcomes. A changed recipe creates a new run; a captured prompt-injection string cannot grant access or schedule work. Unsupported costs/versions are unknown, not zero or invented. (REQ-7, REQ-9, REQ-10)
- [ ] AC-7: Exercise the operations state matrix and all rotation/recovery controls in the companion design. From the human UI inspect a backup checkpoint, a restore verification report, a migration plan with per-source failures and the final-delta/cutover preconditions. Mutation actions require their own capability and a concrete preview. Execute an owner-authorized synthetic rotation through the admin API, observe progress/reconnect, and compare its effects to the CLI protocol; a read-only operations token must be denied. Synthetic fixtures only until deployment is separately authorized. (REQ-8)
- [ ] AC-8: Revoke reader access and verify subsequent reads, indexes, snippets, attachments and exports cannot disclose the revoked scope. Lock clears rendered content and client query caches; responses are no-store. Verify CSRF/origin/session boundaries on mutations and prevent admin or signer privilege through a read-only session. Revocation makes no promise to recall plaintext already copied by a user. (REQ-9, REQ-10)
- [ ] AC-9: Browser tests at desktop, tablet and 390px cover all implemented navigation, filters, keyboard interactions, long identifiers, large paginated lists, inspector open/close, failed fetch, empty/partial results and lock. No body-level horizontal overflow; raw tables may scroll within labeled regions. No external asset requests or executable captured content. (REQ-11)
- [ ] AC-10: Each screen's capability matrix names real API contracts, tests and exact reviewed commits. A UI-only mock or CLI primitive is not marked integrated. Fresh actual Claude Code Opus 5.5 reviews substantive builds/fix rounds; finding fixes include whole-production-fix reversion evidence. (REQ-12)
